clue.text: Second most renowned gardens stink, being crooked

parts.note: Kew Gardens in London are Britain's best-known botanic gardens
a whiff is a bad smell

explanation.surface: A boast that the second most famous gardens smell bad and are dishonestly run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' only links the wordplay to the definition. Kew is the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew or lopsided is colloquially described as off-kilter in this informal British way.

clue.text: Flight of one encased in lead

indicators.note: the one is held inside the word for lead

parts.note: the star of a show plays the lead

explanation.surface: A lone flier whose plane is encased in lead.
explanation.walkthrough: A flight of stairs is a run of steps; one step of it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step is part of a staircase, which is also called a flight.

clue.text: Competitor's fun cut short by storm

definitions.note: read as 'competitor is', so the definition is a noun

indicators.note: the word for fun keeps only its first three letters

parts.note: entertainment is amusement
to rant is to storm about angrily

explanation.surface: A competitor's fun is cut short by bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who signs up for a race or contest is a participant in it.

clue.text: In which the Guardian''s holding 25% cash

indicators.note: the newspaper's word wraps round the letter

parts.note: a newspaper speaks of itself as 'we', so the Guardian's 'we are' contracts to these letters
the last quarter of the four-letter word cash

explanation.surface: A question about which fund holds a quarter of the Guardian's cash.
explanation.definitionFit: This relative adverb introduces the place or situation in which something happens.

clue.text: Elected team's guts

parts.note: a party that is elected is in power
a side is a team, and the possessive supplies the final S

explanation.surface: An elected team said to have guts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' suggests courage; it means the internal organs.
explanation.definitionFit: The innards or internal organs of the body are its entrails.

clue.text: Rattling of teacups is confrontational

definitions.note: the answer is a verb phrase, matching 'is confrontational' only loosely

indicators.note: rattled teacups are shaken about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, part of the jumbled letters
taken as written, the rest of the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: Rattling the teacups is an aggressive way to make a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront a problem or opponent squarely is to meet it head on.

clue.text: Diet? Not the right time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a period of going without food
second meaning: a clock that runs ahead shows the wrong hour

explanation.walkthrough: The clue answer goes into the grid as its opposite, SLOW, which is equally a clock not showing the right time.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from food is a religious or slimming practice, and a clock running ahead is said to be so.

clue.text: Opening to snug as well as taproom is possibly a hazard for sailors

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a snug is a small cosy room in a pub; only its first letter is used
and joins two things in the same way
a taproom is a bar in a pub

explanation.surface: A pub's snug and taproom, possibly dangerous to sailors on shore leave.
explanation.walkthrough: A snug and a taproom are both rooms in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow ridge of sand offshore can ground ships, a classic peril at sea.

clue.text: Nothing in common in these partner-finding web locations?

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a colleague or partner
websites are locations on the web

explanation.surface: Dating websites that pair people with nothing in common.
explanation.walkthrough: Oppo, short for 'opposite number', is British services slang for a mate. The word is also the puzzle's theme: several answers go into the grid as their opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things at either extreme share no qualities, as with black and white.

clue.text: Guarded loose stones that are small in diameter — exactly what's needed

indicators.note: the loose stones are placed in the middle of the other letters

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for diameter, the word made small
'that's it!' is said of exactly the right thing
scree is the loose rock debris on a mountainside

explanation.surface: A geologist describing a guarded heap of fine pebbles that is just the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer goes into the grid as its opposite, TACTLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone careful about what they reveal is reticent and circumspect.

clue.text: Article held by parrot tester

indicators.note: the article sits inside the word for parrot, held by it

parts.note: to parrot is to copy someone's words
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone testing parrots, with an article held by the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A tester is the canopy over a four-poster bed, not someone who tests.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is an old word for the overhead covering on a four-poster bed.

clue.text: No intellectual figure of speech: Penny needs to substitute one

indicators.note: the penny takes the place of the one in the figure of speech

parts.note: a simile is a comparison using like or as
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A literary critic dismissing an unintellectual simile that needs a penny to fix it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer goes into the grid as its opposite, ORNATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is no thinker is plain-minded, naive and unsophisticated.

clue.text: Muscle, having fallen into neglect, is set right

indicators.note: the muscle drops inside the word for neglect

parts.note: disuse is the state of being neglected and unused
ab is short for an abdominal muscle

explanation.surface: A weak muscle, neglected for years, finally corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from a mistaken belief is to correct them about it.

clue.text: Arch stage after measurement reduced

indicators.note: the stage comes after the shortened measurement
the measurement loses its last two letters, cut down

parts.note: an inch is a unit of length
a step is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: A theatre arch whose stage is built once the measurements are cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the raised, arched part of the foot between the toes and the ankle.

clue.text: A good time to remember indulging in it

definitions.text: A good time to remember indulging in it

parts.note: the surface reads as a fond memory of a good time
the 'it' is the wistful longing for that past itself

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the habit of revelling in memories of good times gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sentimental longing for the past and its happy memories.

clue.text: Short-lived romp dissolved into weeping

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go into the word for weeping

parts.note: teary means tearful

indicators.note: something dissolved breaks up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters that are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brief fling that ended in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer goes into the grid as its opposite, PERMANENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brief and passing lasts only for a limited period.

clue.text: United try to get back in lead

indicators.note: the reversed try sits in the middle of the lead

parts.note: a tether is a rope or lead for an animal

indicators.note: the try is turned back to front

parts.note: to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: A football report: United are trying to get back into the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like the football club but is the definition. The answer goes into the grid as its opposite, SEPARATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Things joined in one body are in unison, side by side.

clue.text: Energy soak at Morecambe, comically known to only a few

parts.note: a soak and a sot are both a drunkard
Eric Morecambe was half of the comedy double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A soak at the seaside town of Morecambe, an in-joke few would get.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is also a Lancashire seaside resort, which the surface uses; the wordplay wants the comedian's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is obscure and understood only by a small inner circle.

clue.text: Jacket for pot, old-style marijuana and cocaine on so laid-back, junky's back

parts.note: tea is dated slang for marijuana
C is drug slang for cocaine

indicators.note: laid back here means the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then read backwards

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the junky's back is the last letter of the word junky

explanation.surface: A rambling tale of drugs, with a junky stashing gear in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like cannabis, fitting the drug surface, but it is a teapot.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded cover keeps a teapot warm, a knitted coat for the pot.

clue.text: Whip observed grabbing backside of politician, one used by another

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip

indicators.note: the saw word grabs the letter and holds it inside

parts.note: to have observed something is to have seen it

indicators.note: the backside of a word is its last letter

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A party whip observed grabbing a politician's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' suggests the party official; it is the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: From the fable of the monkey using a cat's paw to pull chestnuts from a fire: a dupe.

clue.text: Three successive characters tip guard

parts.note: D, E, F are consecutive letters of the alphabet
the tip of something is its end

explanation.surface: A puzzle note: three letters in a row then a tip make a guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer goes into the grid as its opposite, OPPOSE, as in proposing and opposing a debate motion.
explanation.definitionFit: To protect something from attack is to shield it.

clue.text: Crucial backing of City turnover by big name

indicators.note: the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: TO is the basketball scoring abbreviation for a turnover
a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: The City's financial turnover backed by a celebrity is crucial.
explanation.walkthrough: City is LA, Los Angeles, not the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on which everything turns is central and decisive.

clue.text: Falls from a rock's pinnacle between Tom and Bill, on going through

indicators.note: the a and the top of rock sit between the two words
the middle letters pass through the gap between the outer words

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a bill passed by parliament becomes an act
taken as written

indicators.note: the pinnacle of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word rock

explanation.surface: A climber falls from a rock pinnacle, landing between two friends called Tom and Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom and Bill look like names but are a cat and a parliamentary bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is a large, steep waterfall.

clue.text: Dull book circle meets climber

parts.note: a circle has the shape of the letter O
a vine is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: A dull book club meets a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bovine literally means cow-like, and so slow-witted and sluggish.

clue.text: Chemist of the "unpleasant odour school"

parts.note: BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A chemist from the 'stinks' school, where chemistry is nicknamed for its smells.
explanation.walkthrough: Carl Bosch was the German chemist of the Haber-Bosch ammonia process.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel-winning German industrial scientist Carl was famous for synthesising ammonia.

clue.text: King's leaving cards seen in churches

indicators.note: the king letter departs from the word for cards

parts.note: knaves are the jacks in a pack of cards
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king; read as 'King is leaving'

explanation.surface: A king walking away from a game of cards to go to church.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the long central halls of churches where the congregation sits.

clue.text: Bill's rather obvious description of meltwater?

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill stating the obvious about meltwater.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer goes into the grid as its opposite, IGNORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a poster or printed announcement put up for the public.

clue.text: Original image, say, possessed by aboriginal?

indicators.note: the abbreviation is held inside the word for aboriginal

parts.note: a native is an original inhabitant
eg, for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'

explanation.surface: An aboriginal people owning an original artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: In film photography the developed film is the original from which prints are made. The answer goes into the grid as its opposite, POSITIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: In film photography the developed strip with reversed tones is the master from which every print is made.

clue.text: Severe shiver on removing top

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken off

parts.note: a shiver is a splinter or fragment, like a shard

explanation.surface: A severe shiver once the top layer of clothing comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shiver' suggests trembling; here it is the noun for a splinter. The answer goes into the grid as its opposite, EASY.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh, demanding regime or winter is tough and stern.

clue.text: Tense, admit greetings should exclude round public buildings

parts.note: to own up is to admit

indicators.note: the round letter is left out of the greetings

parts.note: hallo is a greeting
a round thing is shaped like the letter O
